title: Dispatcher memory leak and connection-window exhaustion — investigation & mitigation
author: Maya Singh
body:
Summary
-------
This page documents a recurring failure class observed in the dispatcher service where long-running connection windows and an unbounded buffer growth lead to pod memory exhaustion and partial request loss. The doc covers: detection signals, short-term mitigations, permanent fixes planned, rollout steps, post-incident verification, and ownership.

Context and scope
------------------
- Affected service: dispatcher-service (grpc frontend + connection multiplexer)
- Secondary impact: kernel-manager and grpc-proxy pods observed elevated tail latency due to request drops and retries.
- Customer-visible symptoms: increased 5xx rates on hosted API routes, transient model swap failures, and elevated p99 latency.
- Root hypothesis summary: under sustained backpressure (long KV cache fetches / slow kernel warmstarts), the dispatcher accumulates connection windows and request buffers that are not compacted, causing memory pressure and eventual OOM/kube eviction.

Why this matters
------------------
- SLO impact: incidents breached the 99.9% availability SLO for several customer routes for 4–17 minutes in observed incidents.
- Cost/operational: repeated restarts mask the underlying problem and create downstream load spikes (thundering herd) when services recover.

Detection and alerting
----------------------
Create or verify these signals in Grafana / Prometheus: 
1) Memory growth slope alert (dispatcher pod level):
- PromQL (example):
  increase(container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="dispatcher-service"}[15m]) > 150e6
- Alert intent: signal sustained memory growth > 150MB over 15 minutes.

2) Connection-window count spike:
- Instrumentation metric: dispatcher_connection_windows_total (gauge of active per-client windows)
- PromQL: sum(dispatcher_connection_windows_total) by(cluster_zone) > 5000

3) Request buffer backlog:
- Metric: dispatcher_request_buffer_depth (histogram buckets or gauge). Alert when avg > 400 per pod for 10m.

4) Error surface correlation: correlate 500s spike with buffer metrics using dashboards. Create a combined panel that shows: 5xx_rate, dispatcher_memory_working_set, request_buffer_depth

Investigation checklist (fast triage)
------------------------------------
1) Identify affected pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=dispatcher-service --field-selector status.phase!=Running
2) Check last OOM reason: kubectl describe pod <pod> | grep -i oom
3) Check top memory consumers inside the pod: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- pmap /proc/1/maps || ps aux --sort=-rss | head -n 20
4) Query metrics: use the PromQL alerts above to identify trend and onset time windows.
5) Grab heap profile (if enabled): curl -sS http://<pod-ip>:6060/debug/pprof/heap > heap-<pod>.pb.gz
6) Correlate with kernel-manager traces: tracer id / request ids in logs. Use the trace-id header to find full request timeline.

Immediate mitigations (stop-gap, low-risk)
------------------------------------------
Apply these in order to reduce customer-visible impact while preserving diagnostics: 
1) Scale horizontally: kubectl scale --replicas=+2 deploy/dispatcher-service (add pods to lower per-pod backlog).
2) Enable admission backpressure: set config dispatcher.max_inflight_per_client to 50 (from default 200) via config map and rolling restart. This limits per-client window growth.
3) TTL/Compaction: reduce dispatcher.window_idle_ttl from 10m to 90s to force faster window tear-down.
4) Controlled rolling restart: restart the pods with highest memory slope first, one at a time, with 3m drain between restarts. Use the readiness probe to ensure no traffic is sent to the pod during restart.
5) Route heavy customers to Dedicated capacity or lower-priority model variants temporarily (use routing policy to steer by customer tag).

Permanent remediation plan (engineering work items)
--------------------------------------------------
Priority and owner: platform/runtime team (owner: Maya Singh)
Planned tasks and rationale: 
- Task A (P0): Fix buffer compaction logic — when downstream kernels take long to accept data, dispatcher should compact or spill oldest requests to disk-backed buffer with explicit backpressure. (PR: #5482)
- Task B (P1): Add bounded request queue per-client with adaptive eviction policies (evict smallest/least-progressing items).
- Task C (P1): Improve heap visibility — enable continuous heap sampling and add an automated heap-diff alert with sample retention for 72 hours.
- Task D (P2): Add a new telemetry label to trace all requests carrying dispatcher_window_id for easier cross-service correlation.
- Task E (P2): Scheduler change — enforce admission controls earlier in edge proxies to stop untrusted clients from opening many logical windows.
Estimated timeline: P0 in 3 weeks (hotfix + canary), P1/P2 in 6–10 weeks with review cycles and integration tests.

Patch / hotfix notes
--------------------
- Hotfix branches: hotfix/dispatcher/buffer-compact-2026-06 (contains limited compaction and conservative defaults).
- Canary plan: deploy to canary zone (us-west-canary) with 5% traffic shadowing for 48 hours and run the playback suite from benchmarking repo (endpoint: /health-playback).
- PR references: #5482 (compaction), #5510 (window-id telemetry).

Rollout checklist (post-PR merge)
--------------------------------
1) Deploy hotfix to staging and run the synthetic backlog test from benchmarking suite: benchmarks/runtime/dispatcher-backlog-sim (expected max memory < 1.2x baseline).
2) Canary deploy to us-west-canary with traffic-split=5% and monitor alerts for 24–48 hours.
3) If no regressions, lift to 25% traffic for another 24 hours.
4) Gradually roll to remaining regions with guardrails: watch for memory-slope alert, request_buffer_depth, and 5xx_rate.
5) Complete rollout and mark release in release-tracker: release-id: rdr-runtime-2026-06-compact.

Rollback plan
-------------
- If memory slope increases by > 50% vs baseline or 5xx rate increases > 1% absolute during canary: rollback to previous deploy using kubectl rollout undo deployment/dispatcher-service --to-revision=<rev> and revert config changes (max_inflight_per_client, window_idle_ttl).
- For severe regressions, scale down the hotfix replicas and revert config through the operator to restore previous behavior.

Post-incident verification and monitoring additions
--------------------------------------------------
- Add a derived metric: dispatcher_active_window_memory_ratio = dispatcher_memory_used_by_windows / container_memory_working_set_bytes. Alert if > 0.6 for 10m.
- Add an automated dashboard row in the dispatcher incident dashboard: memory slope, buffer depth, active windows, 5xx rate, kernel-manager inflight.
- Add unit and integration tests in the runtime bench suite that simulate slow kernel acceptance and verify compaction does not exceed memory targets.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owner: Runtime Platform (oncall rotation: runtime-platform-oncall).
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime SRE.
- Pager escalation: runtime-platform-oncall -> platform-lead -> eng-sre-lead.
- Slack channels: #runtime-ops, #serving-incident-escalations

Postmortem and follow-ups
-------------------------
1) Run a two-week incident review with stakeholders: runtime, SRE, kernel-team, customer-success for any impacted customers.
2) Deliver a short RCA doc that enumerates timeline, root causes, and action items with target dates.
3) Close or convert any temporary mitigations (shorter TTLs, stricter admission) into configuration toggles that default to safe values.

Appendices
---------
A) Example PromQL snippets
- Memory slope (per pod): increase(container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"dispatcher-service-.*"}[10m])
- Buffer depth agg: avg_over_time(dispatcher_request_buffer_depth[5m])
- Combined alert rule sample:
  - name: DispatcherMemorySlope
    expr: increase(container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="dispatcher-service"}[15m]) > 150e6
    for: 10m

B) Diagnostic commands
1) pod list and memory usage: kubectl top pod -n inference | grep dispatcher-service\2) fetch heap profile: kubectl exec -n inference -c dispatcher <pod> -- curl -sS localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap.pb.gz\3) extract top alloc sites from heap: go tool pprof -top /tmp/heap.pb.gz\\n
C) Impact table (sample from incident 2026-06-18)
| Region | Duration | Peak affected pods | Customer routes impacted | Notes |
| us-west-2 | 00:17 | 3 | /v1/generate, /v1/chat | sustained KV fetch failure from remote cache |
| eu-central-1 | 00:04 | 1 | /v1/embed | transient kernel warmstart stutter |

Contact and next steps
----------------------
If you are paged, follow the Investigation checklist, apply Immediate mitigations as needed, and notify runtime-platform-oncall. For changes to telemetry or alerting, open an RFC in the runtime-team repo and tag reviewers: @EthanB, @LeahM.
